content.title: About
content.content: Cooked carrots are the root vegetable that has been boiled or steamed until tender. Most nutrients are retained during cooking, while the natural sugars become sweeter and the texture softens. Cooked carrots are common in soups, stews, salads, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots have been cultivated for over 5,000 years, originating in Central Asia.
The orange variety was developed in the Netherlands in the 17th century through selective breeding.
Raw carrots can be purple, yellow, red, or white; orange became dominant due to its high beta‑carotene content.
Cooking makes beta‑carotene more bioavailable for conversion to vitamin A.
Carrots are used in traditional medicine to support vision and immune health.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A, essential for eye health, skin, and immune function.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and potassium help regulate blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin C protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fiber promote healthy gut motility.

items.title: May reduce chronic disease risk
items.content: Regular carrot consumption is linked to lower risk of certain cancers and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to carrots.

items.title: Excess vitamin A
items.content: Very large intakes of carrots can lead to hypervitaminosis A, causing a yellowish skin tone.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs may experience gas when eating large amounts of cooked carrots.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked carrots can be served as a side, added to salads, purees, soups, and stews. They are also used in baking (e.g., carrot cake) and in juices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked carrots in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags to retain flavor and nutrients.
